titulo: Introductions, countries, numbers 0-20 and age: Introducing yourself

aula.objetivo: Introduce yourself and others, ask and say where someone is from, name countries and nationalities, count from 0 to 20 and say your age with «ter».

blocos.titulo: Meeting people: names, origin and the polite «you»
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: you can say your name in three ways, all very common: «Eu sou Marina», «Meu nome é Marina» or «Eu me chamo Marina». After the introduction, the other person says «Prazer!» or «Muito prazer!», and you answer «Prazer!» or «Igualmente!». STEP 2: to ask for a name, use «Qual é o seu nome?» (literally «which is your name?») or «Como você se chama?» (literally «how do you call yourself?»). Learn both as whole phrases for now: «meu» and «seu» (my, your) come in lesson 7, and verbs like «se chamar» in lesson 14. STEP 3: to ask where someone is from, say «De onde você é?». The answer is «Sou de…» followed by a city: «Sou de São Paulo». With countries it is a little different, and you will see it in the next session. STEP 4: to introduce another person, say «Este é Pedro» (a man) and «Esta é Ana» (a woman). It means «this is». STEP 5: «o senhor» (to a man) and «a senhora» (to a woman) are the polite way to say «you», for older people, in a formal service, with a boss or with someone you have just met in a formal setting. The verb is the same as for «você»: «O senhor é médico?», «A senhora é de onde?». Among friends and in most casual situations use «você». STEP 6: for older people you can also use «Seu» (short for «senhor») or «Dona» before the first name: «Seu José», «Dona Marta». It is respectful and warm, not cold. STEP 7: in a formal or first meeting people often shake hands. Among friends and acquaintances, especially with women, a kiss on the cheek or a hug is common, and the number of kisses varies by region. Follow the other person's lead.
blocos.comparacao: In English one «you» works for the king and for your best friend. In Portuguese the choice of «você» or «o senhor/a senhora» tells how formal the situation is. Do not worry: «você» is correct almost everywhere in Brazil. English «How do you do?» is more formal than Portuguese «Prazer», which people use all the time, even with young colleagues. Also note the question «De onde você é?»: the verb is «ser» (to be from), not «vir».

exemplos.pt: Hi, I am Marina. Nice to meet you!
Nice to meet you, Pedro. — Likewise!

exemplos.ru: De onde você é? — Sou de São Paulo.
exemplos.pt: Where are you from? — I am from São Paulo.

exemplos.ru: Esta é Ana. Este é Rafael.
exemplos.pt: This is Ana. This is Rafael.

tabela.situation: a friend, a classmate, a colleague
an older acquaintance, warm and respectful

erros.motivo: The subject is «nome», so the verb is «é». «Sou» goes only with «eu».
«Me chamo» is one expression. Do not add «sou».
The «se» is part of the expression.
«De nada» answers «obrigado». To a «prazer» you answer «prazer» or «igualmente».

blocos.enunciado: Do a short role play out loud. First with a friend: say your name, ask the name, answer «Prazer!», ask where they are from. Then do it again in a polite way with «o senhor» or «a senhora».
Say the present of «ser» aloud. Then say who you are with your profession (for example «Eu sou estudante»), describe a friend with two adjectives, and make one negative sentence.
